cohort: 387 term pregnant women aged 18-40 from a tertiary care center in Saudi Arabia, divided into those who received epidural analgesia and controls.
finding: Epidural analgesia was not significantly associated with an increased rate of emergency cesarean sections or adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: While initial analysis linked epidural analgesia to higher emergency C-sections, multivariable analysis showed no significant effect on C-section or instrumental delivery rates.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome, found to be similar between groups.
